problem: No official intersection map available
impact: Absolute layout (lanes, crosswalks, stop lines) unverified for both sensors

problem: Persistent static "Pedestrian" (and Cyclist/Motorcycle) detections at fixed points; largest hotspot (Ouster-world -25,+1) = K1 signal head/pole, ~1 detection per frame for 83 min. Audit: 281,711 of 489,744 NS PED observations lie in the 10 hotspot cells; outside them NS/OU = 1.15; only the K1-pole hotspot is video-checked
affected_period: all hours analysed (28 and 29 Oct 06-13; measured in 29 Oct 07:12-08:35 (common period))
impact: Inflates pedestrian counts/density at fixed points; 85 % of unconfirmed NS pedestrian detections are stationary, 78 % in 10 cells
proposed_correction: Symmetric stationarity/hotspot sensitivity analysis (report with/without); video-check remaining hotspots; no deletion of detections
correction_applied: None yet (filter to be defined and validated in C3)
remaining_uncertainty: Hotspots (-19,+3), (-17,+3) adjacent to K1: no person in 4 decidable round-2 frames; (-25,+1) K1 pole re-confirmed 3/3; (-9,-17) undecidable; level 2.4x higher on 29 Oct than 28 Oct (C6)
affects_fairness: Yes - raw NS pedestrian counts are not comparable without filtering
fairness_preservation: Any spatial/stationarity filter applied identically to both sensors with the same thresholds

problem: Same physical point reported simultaneously as two classes (< 0.3 m): 24.7 pairs per 1000 detections (Ouster 1.3); at track level 628 persistent pairs (>= 10 frames, median 21): Cyclist+Pedestrian 375, Cyclist+Motorcycle 171, Motorcycle+Pedestrian 82 (Ouster: 1)
affected_period: 29 Oct 07:12-08:35 (common period) (region); other hours not yet quantified
impact: Double counting of VRUs
proposed_correction: Count co-located multi-class VRU pairs as one object in object-level counts (sensitivity)
fairness_preservation: Same co-location rule applied to Ouster (PERSON/BICYCLE/UNKNOWN)

problem: Track fragmentation: interruptions become new ids. Moving-track breaks with a nearby continuation per robust km (T = 2 s): PED 33.4 vs Ouster 20.8; CYC 28.5 vs 9.1 (Cyclist + Motorcycle; Cyclist label only 33.9; V1 value 20.9 withdrawn, CORR-02); VEH 5.7 vs 1.7. Magnitude depends on how Ouster UNKNOWN fragments are attributed (PED 1.2-1.9x, VEH 2.0-3.4x); the direction holds in every variant. 21 % of moving NS vehicle tracks start inside the region (Ouster 1.5 %)
impact: Under-estimates trajectory length; inflates track counts
proposed_correction: Track-stitching ANALYSIS (space-time continuity) for both sensors; compare total path rather than per-track medians
affects_fairness: Yes - track counts not comparable directly
fairness_preservation: Stitching applied to both sensors with identical gap/distance limits

problem: score = 1.0 for every object on 28 Oct but 0.20-0.45 (medians) on 29 Oct: semantics changed between days (with the frame-phase change, suggests software/config change)
impact: Score not usable as a consistent confidence across days

problem: Velocity initialised at exactly 0 in 99.7 % of tracks, then ramps over ~5 samples (0, 1.9, 3.1, 3.8, 4.2, 4.4 m/s median for moving tracks)
impact: Start-of-track metrics not comparable; first velocity samples unreliable
proposed_correction: Exclude the first 5 samples (0.5 s) of every Newsense track from velocity metrics
fairness_preservation: Exclusion length reported; Ouster first samples tested for the same artefact

problem: Frequent class-label changes within tracks (75 % of pedestrian, 42 % of cyclist, 27 % of vehicle tracks in common region; typically UNKNOWN -> class); 97 % of PED tracks in full coverage
impact: Per-detection class counts depend on time within track
proposed_correction: Use dominant/final label per track; report label-transition statistics
correction_applied: Dominant label per track used for track metrics
fairness_preservation: Dominant-label rule applied to both (Newsense never switches)

problem: Coasted (predicted, not measured) objects: num_points 0 / update_ts older than frame; 1.5-2.4 % of VRU/vehicle and 17.6 % of UNKNOWN detections in common region; lower cross-sensor confirmation
impact: Some reported positions are predictions
proposed_correction: Report with and without coasted samples
fairness_preservation: Newsense has no coasting flag -> reported as a transparency difference, not removed from one side only in headline numbers

problem: UNKNOWN class = mix of real persons, vehicle fragments and clutter; 70 % of UNKNOWN tracks < 1 s; 46 % of UNKNOWN tracks never confirmed by Newsense
impact: Real VRUs can be hidden in UNKNOWN; clutter inflates object counts
remaining_uncertainty: Share of real VRUs in UNKNOWN
fairness_preservation: Bounds reported; Newsense has no UNKNOWN class (forced classes) - stated

problem: Pedestrian positions show 1-2 m discontinuities within one frame (0.1 s). Share of PED tracks with a jump is threshold-dependent: 22.2 % (step speed > 12 m/s and > 1 m, C2), 23.9 % (dominant-label limit), 6.2 % (> 2 m), 5.8 % (> 20 m/s), 1.4 % (> 3 m); 32 % of C2-definition jumps involve a coasted sample; 0 from timestamp jitter. Newsense: 0 under all definitions (likely upstream filtering/segmentation, see NS-12/NS-14)
impact: Noisier Ouster pedestrian trajectories at 1-2 m scale; affects speed/conflict indicators; smoothness is not accuracy
proposed_correction: Report jump rates for several thresholds and per km / per track-hour; separate coasted samples
fairness_preservation: Identical thresholds and coordinate frame for both sensors

problem: Ouster-only (unconfirmed) PED: C2 detection-weighted sample 0/12 confirmed (4 decidable); round-2 track-level sample 3/8 confirmed (3 of 4 decidable) - some Ouster-only moving pedestrians are real persons missed by Newsense. Not a false-positive rate
impact: False-positive status of unconfirmed Ouster pedestrians unresolved
fairness_preservation: Same sampling frame and protocol for both sensors

problem: Both sensors timestamps are ~2.8 s later than the Stage 3 v2 video-derived reference for the same motion: 2.81 s (sample sd 0.12, 6 all-object scans in 3 windows; all 10 scans 2.59-2.94 s); robust to homography (v2/v3/v4) and travel direction. CAUSE UNKNOWN: "export detector columns lag state columns" is NOT supported (loop release 4-5 s argues against a full 2.8 s detector lag; sensor start-up 3.2-4.6 s after export green is ambiguous)
affected_period: measured 29 Oct 07:20-07:30, 07:40-07:50, 08:10-08:20; assumed for whole common period
impact: Video-sensor alignment off by ~2.8 s if Stage 3 v2 is used alone; Stage 3 statement "Newsense ~ signal" holds only for detector columns
proposed_correction: Decisive video-internal start-up test (queue head vs visible lamp green) compared with sensor start-up vs export green; request export convention (SG-01). No clock model change before that
correction_applied: None to data; offset used for video look-ups only; clock_model_v2 unchanged
remaining_uncertainty: Which clock is "true"; export internal timing
fairness_preservation: Affects both sensors equally; only video look-ups use the offset
revision: v3 (C2 audit): correctable, correction_applied, evidence, problem

problem: Ground-plane registration only approximate (stationary-object homography, ~10-35 px on independent frames); haze/glare limits visibility at the left image edge
impact: Video verification is object-level and indicative (n=12 per category, single rater)

problem: Video sample was detection-weighted (static objects over-represented: 6 of 12 NS tiles from one 10 m cell) and restricted to the camera view (30/60 NS, 32/60 OU reservoir items outside)
impact: Video rates describe observations in the visible area, not tracks or objects overall
proposed_correction: Stratified sample by track, cell and time; >= 2 raters
fairness_preservation: Same sampling frame for both sensors

problem: Headline NS/OU pedestrian ratio 2.53 is in observations (object x frame); moving > 0.3 m/s 1.12, > 0.5 m/s 0.80, moving tracks 0.91, outside hotspots 1.15; jitter-robust moving path 0.67 (CORR-01; the earlier "total path 1.00" was a jitter artefact)
impact: Unitless ratios mislead about real pedestrian detection
correction_applied: All ratios now reported with unit and definition

problem: Region-scope "ID reuse" counted objects leaving and re-entering the region (> 5 s) as reuse (NS region 766 > NS full coverage 730)
impact: Metric mixes geometry with tracker behaviour
proposed_correction: Full-coverage definition: same id reappearing after > 5 s gap or > 15 m in <= 1 s, counted in each sensor own footprint
correction_applied: Recomputed on full coverage (C3 s2.1; wording corrected in C3 v3): Newsense 639 ids reused for other objects + 59 instantaneous swaps; Ouster 0 + 0; Ouster 359 id re-attachments after 5-30 s (vendor re-find flag; same object not verified)

problem: Pair metrics (position residual, speed difference) shown as two per-sensor columns with identical values
impact: Readers may assume independent per-sensor measurements

problem: Track identifiers are recycled: 639 ids re-used for a different object in 83 min (636 after > 60 s: median 19 min, 35 m away, class differs in 85 %; 3 after 15-58 s, 25-38 m away with class change) and 59 instantaneous id swaps (> 15 m within 1 s, vehicle <-> cyclist, 98 % simultaneous with another swap)
impact: Id is not a unique object key; naive per-id analyses merge different objects
proposed_correction: Same segmentation for any downstream use
correction_applied: Segmentation (gap > 5 s, jump > 15 m) used in all C2-C3 track metrics
affects_fairness: Yes - handled by identical segmentation for both sensors

problem: Ids persist across short losses: 359 re-attachments after 5-30 s (median 7 m, same class 97 %), all carrying Ouster's own refind_time flag; a further ~1,400 gaps of 1-5 s are bridged inside ids; no id recycling within 84 min (ids monotonic)
impact: Positive for id stability: ids are re-attached across short losses (same physical object not verified); gap samples absent (no interpolation)
correction_applied: Treated as new segment for gap > 5 s (same rule as Newsense)
remaining_uncertainty: Whether every re-attachment is the same physical object (only 31 % same class and within 5 m)
revision: v4 (final-package audit): evidence, impact, problem, remaining_uncertainty

problem: Track-break / continuation counts depend on the gap window (T = 1-3 s) and family rule; stitching is an analysis of fragmentation, not a correction of the data
impact: Fragmentation numbers are indicative, given with sensitivity
remaining_uncertainty: Dense pedestrian groups can create spurious links

problem: Raw path length (sum of all position steps) is inflated by position jitter of stationary objects: 9.15 of 21.75 km NS pedestrian path comes from objects reporting < 0.3 m/s, 8.51 km lies in the 10 hotspot cells. "Equal total pedestrian path (1.00)" was an artefact
impact: The C2-audit statement and C3 v1 per-km rates were wrong; corrected: robust moving path PED 0.67, CYC 1.04 only when NS Motorcycle is counted as cyclist (Cyclist label only 0.64; PED + CYC 0.83), VEH 0.90 (NS/OU)
correction_applied: Jitter-robust path (1 s decimation, >= 0.5 m) used from C3 v2 on; originals preserved
remaining_uncertainty: Robust path still counts Ouster moving fragments/merges as movement
affects_fairness: Yes - the raw measure favoured the sensor with static jitter
fairness_preservation: Same robust rule for both sensors

problem: PET v1 counted same-direction following (e.g. cyclists in the vehicle path) as encroachment: Ouster PET < 2 s moving 85 (v1) vs 19 (v2, crossing angle >= 30 deg); Newsense 20 vs 12
impact: v1 PET counts inflated, mostly for Ouster cyclists
correction_applied: C7 v2 (crossing angle >= 30 deg); v1 kept

problem: Severe surrogate conflict events (TTC < 1.5 s, PET < 2 s, moving VRU) are similar in number per sensor (31 vs 35; 12 vs 19) but mostly different events: 6-42 % have an event of the same kind at any level in the other sensor (TTC 7/31 and 4/35); severe in both sensors: TTC 1/31 and 1/35, PET 4/12 and 4/19
impact: Event-level safety analysis is sensor-dependent; single-sensor conflict lists are not reproducible
proposed_correction: Clip-based multi-rater video review of the 66 severe TTC and 31 severe PET candidates

problem: Stationary Newsense VRUs dominate interaction indicators: 789 TTC < 3 s events with stationary NS "pedestrians" (Ouster 193); 388 of the 789 (49 %) lie in the 10 hotspot cells where static false objects are documented (one video-confirmed); the other events are not shown to be spurious and may include real waiting pedestrians
impact: Unfiltered Newsense conflict counts are inflated by static false objects (extent outside the hotspots unknown)
proposed_correction: Exclude stationary VRU events or video-check them
affects_fairness: Yes - handled by separating states for both sensors

problem: At track level (middle sample of moving tracks, stratified by time and image zone) SCU3K2 video rarely decides: control (both sensors agree) 0/12 confirmed (5 ambiguous, 3 cannot verify, 2 occluded); far field and image edges are hazy
impact: Video cannot serve as a general reference for detection rates in this view; C2 control 8/12 was favoured by detection weighting
proposed_correction: Clip-based review; near-field strata; second rater

dataset: CORR-01c / C3 v2 / final package V1
problem: Newsense cyclist break rate per robust km divided Cyclist-only links by Cyclist + Motorcycle km (20.9 at T = 2 s)
impact: Cyclist fragmentation difference understated (2.3x instead of 3.1-3.7x); direction unchanged
correction_applied: CORR-02: consistent classes (28.5 Cyclist + Motorcycle, 33.9 Cyclist only); V2 figures, tables, slides and register corrected; V1 kept
fairness_preservation: Same class set in numerator and denominator for both sensors

problem: Final package V1 over-stated or mislabelled several results: agreement "flagged by both sensors" (definition: any level in the other sensor); all 789 stationary events called "spurious"; "same object re-acquired" (vendor re-find, identity unverified); "637 ids > 60 s" (636 > 60 s; 639 reused in total); NS "2 re-acquisitions" (recycled ids); cyclist 1.04x without stating that NS Motorcycle is included; fixed fragmentation magnitudes; "66 severe candidates" (TTC only); slide 18 labels; F06 without the movement measure; stale "pedestrians similar" in C3 v2
impact: Some claims stronger than the evidence; no headline conclusion reversed
correction_applied: Corrected in final package V2, C3 v3, C7 v3, CORR-01 v2; V1 kept
affects_fairness: Partly (wording favoured Ouster on identity, Newsense on cyclist similarity)
fairness_preservation: Same wording rules for both sensors

problem: C1 generalised a stationary-vehicle location statistic (22 % of sampled stationary NS vehicle observations unmatched and in cells without Ouster vehicle-class detections) to "Ouster coverage is smaller than Newsense's" (now withdrawn), contradicting C1 s11 (footprint 3.5x)
impact: Contradiction between C1 and the final package; no number affected
correction_applied: Versioned C1 correction note 01; C1 report not edited
remaining_uncertainty: Whether the local Newsense-only stationary vehicles are real (U-02)

problem: Counts with thresholds on the 0.1 s sampling grid are tie-sensitive: PET < 2 s 12/19 vs 13/20 and Ouster re-attachments 359 vs 360 depending on timestamp rounding (ms vs 0.1 ms); decimation-based robust path varies by about 1 %
impact: +-1 event or about 1 % in affected numbers; no conclusion affected
proposed_correction: Thresholds off the sampling grid in future work (e.g. <= 1.95 s)

problem: The final-package audit re-implemented key calculations from raw data but was carried out by the same analyst as the original analysis; it is not an independent external review. Several results were not re-implemented (C2 matching shares, classification confusion, double labels, durations, jump shares, C4, C5/C6, video labels, CK-01)
impact: Shared conceptual errors could survive; the package is not fully scientifically validated
proposed_correction: External reviewer re-runs final_audit/scripts and the original scripts
